correctness.rationale: PASS: Prüfer coding makes the leaf count n-j equivalent to exactly j occupied labels in an N=n-2 word. Conditioning gives P(X_j=c)=binom(N,c) S(N-c,j-1)/(n S(N,j)) (c>=1), and P(X_j=0)=(n-j)/n, with fixed EX_j=N/n. Size-bias gives q_j(c)=binom(N-1,c-1)S(N-c,j-1)/S(N,j). Real-rooted Bell polynomials imply log-concave Stirling coefficients; the Stirling recurrence proves strictly decreasing S(t,r-1)/S(t,r) in t. Therefore q_{j-1}/q_j increases in c (with endpoint support), yielding strict stochastic order of size biases. The increasing secant-slope representation transfers it into strict convex order of degrees and the covariance consequences. Independently enumerated all Prüfer words for n=4..7 (16,125,1296,16807), checking every adjacent conditional convex-hinge comparison. The universal conclusion rests on the recurrence proof.
